claims.text: The starting material consists of crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles containing five or more metals.
Using a high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle is a distinct intervention relative to the stated starting material.
A high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle can retain a multielement solid solution.
Such nanoparticles have potential catalytic performance at low noble-metal content.
Merely using a high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle could overcome instability during catalytic operation at 773–1173 K.
The intervention is intended for catalytic operation in the 773–1173 K range.
The structural mediator is the high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle itself.
A high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle provides a stable catalytic surface.
A high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle provides an active catalytic surface.
The stable and active surface results from the multielement solid solution and low noble-metal content.
The intervention will improve stability relative to untreated nanoparticles during operation at 773–1173 K.
The intervention will improve catalytic performance relative to untreated nanoparticles during operation at 773–1173 K.
The exact alloy composition and structure may affect the outcome.
Specific operating conditions may affect the outcome.

contradictions.description: The starting material and baseline are already multielement high-entropy-style solid-solution nanoparticles, while the proposed intervention is simply to use a high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle. No actual modification of the baseline is specified.
The outcome and falsification rule require improvement relative to untreated nanoparticles, but the proposed intervention does not distinguish the treated material from the stated untreated baseline.
